combinations.name: MAOIs
combinations.description: An MAOI removes the main way your body clears released monoamines, so blood pressure can spike into a crisis. Meth's strength and long duration make the margin even thinner than amphetamine. Do not combine.

combinations.name: Alcohol
combinations.description: The stimulant hides how drunk you are, so alcohol gets redosed too far — and meth's long duration outlasts most drinking. Heart strain adds up even when you can't feel it.

combinations.name: Other stimulants
combinations.description: Cocaine, MDMA, more amphetamine — heart rate and blood pressure add together, and meth already sits near the top. Stacking raises the strain faster than the effect.

combinations.name: Opioids
combinations.description: The stimulant hides opioid drowsiness, the usual warning of too much — so a heavy opioid dose can feel manageable until the meth wears off first. If combining, dose the opioid as if the meth weren't there.

waterHeat.headline: Sip to thirst
waterHeat.body: Stimulants blunt thirst without changing how much fluid you need — not much more than usual unless you're moving hard or in the heat. Sip to thirst; don't force water. On a long session, remember to eat.
